question: What is the main focus of primary health care delivery?
explanation: Primary health care focuses heavily on stopping illness before it starts through prevention and health promotion within communities. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T2#BMP110_U2_T2_h1)

question: Which tier of government in Nigeria is primarily responsible for managing primary health care facilities?
explanation: Local Government Health Authorities handle the day-to-day administration and running of primary health facilities at the grassroots. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T2#BMP110_U2_T2_h1)

question: How are primary health facilities in Nigeria generally structured?

options.A: As single large hospitals located in every village
options.B: Exclusively as private pharmacies in urban areas
options.C: In a tiered pyramid from community to comprehensive centres
options.D: As mobile clinics with no fixed locations

explanation: The system uses a graded network of facilities to match the complexity of care needed with the right level of facility. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T2#BMP110_U2_T2_h2)

question: Why is a tiered facility structure important for rural healthcare delivery?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any secondary or tertiary hospitals
options.B: It forces all patients to travel to cities for basic checkups
options.C: It ensures patients receive care at the simplest appropriate level first
options.D: It prevents community health workers from seeing pregnant women

explanation: Stepped structures prevent higher-level facilities from getting overcrowded with minor health issues that local posts can easily handle. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T2#BMP110_U2_T2_h2)

question: What defines a health post within the primary health care structure?

options.A: It is a large facility equipped with major surgical theatres
options.B: It is the most basic unit located closest to rural communities
options.C: It is a mobile laboratory for advanced blood testing
options.D: It is an urban hospital handling complex specialist referrals

explanation: Health posts sit at the very bottom of the healthcare pyramid to serve remote populations directly. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T2#BMP110_U2_T2_h3)

question: Which type of personnel typically staffs a standard rural health post?

options.D: Community health workers and trained volunteers

explanation: Because of their remote locations, health posts rely on lower-cadre frontline workers to provide basic community interventions. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T2#BMP110_U2_T2_h3)

question: Which healthcare worker commonly manages a standard primary health clinic in Nigeria?
explanation: CHEWs form the backbone of staffing for primary health clinics and basic health centres across rural and semi-urban settlements. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T2#BMP110_U2_T2_h4)

question: What feature distinguishes a basic health centre from a smaller health clinic?

options.A: Exclusive focus on treating dental disorders
options.B: Presence of observation beds for short stays
options.C: Exemption from keeping any medical records

explanation: Health centres usually have simple observation wards where patients can be monitored for a few hours before discharge or transfer. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T2#BMP110_U2_T2_h4)

question: What is a key capability of a Comprehensive Health Centre?

options.A: Conducting only home visits for health education
options.D: Providing 24-hour maternity and minor surgical services

explanation: CHCs are equipped and staffed to handle round-the-clock emergencies, including childbirth complications and minor operations. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T2#BMP110_U2_T2_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT typically found in a basic health post but IS found in a Comprehensive Health Centre?

options.A: Basic health education posters on the walls
options.B: Resident medical officers and comprehensive laboratories

explanation: Basic health posts do not have doctors or full diagnostic laboratories, whereas CHCs are staffed and equipped with these advanced resources. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T2#BMP110_U2_T2_h5)

question: What is the primary responsibility of a midwife stationed at a primary health facility?

options.A: Managing normal pregnancies and attending to childbirth

explanation: Midwives are trained specifically to care for women during pregnancy, labor, and the postnatal period to ensure safe deliveries. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T2#BMP110_U2_T2_h6)

question: Why is a multidisciplinary team necessary at a primary health facility?

options.A: It allows doctors to avoid working in rural areas completely
options.B: Different cadres bring specialized skills to address diverse community needs
options.C: Government regulations forbid any single worker from opening a clinic
options.D: It ensures that nurses never have to perform administrative duties

explanation: Primary care involves everything from sanitation to childbirth, requiring a mix of nursing, community health, and environmental expertise. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T2#BMP110_U2_T2_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of a medical referral system?

options.A: To increase the cost of healthcare for rural dwellers
options.B: To reduce the number of patients visiting any hospital
options.C: To punish health workers who make mistakes
options.D: To transfer complicated cases to higher-level facilities

explanation: Referrals ensure patients who need advanced medical or surgical care are moved safely to a hospital equipped to handle them. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T2#BMP110_U2_T2_h7)

question: A midwife at a primary health centre encounters a woman with severe prolonged labor and fetal distress. What immediate step should she take?

options.A: Discharge the patient with advice to rest at home
options.B: Initiate an emergency referral to a secondary health facility
options.C: Wait until morning to see if the baby delivers naturally
options.D: Attempt a major surgical procedure in the clinic

explanation: Severe complications like prolonged labor surpass primary care capabilities and require urgent transfer to a facility with surgical capacity. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T2#BMP110_U2_T2_h7)
